rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward return moves from natural impulses toward intellect, then from witnessing acts through attributes to knowledge of the divine essence.
rows.anchor: أي رجاع عما حطه عنه طبعه إلى ما يعليه إليه عقله , فيرجع من شهود هذه الأفعال إلى شهود هذه الصفات إلى علم الذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descent of water is a foremost sign of God, who cannot be described as inside or outside, connected to or separate from the world.
rows.anchor: إنزال الماء أبهر الآيات وأدلها على أنه أجل من أن يقال : إنه داخل العالم أو خارجه , أو متصل به أو منفصل عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water produces vegetation and provisions, and through it every living thing has life.
rows.anchor: مع أن به تكون النبات وحصول الأقوات وبه حياة كل شيء , أفرده تنبيها على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends water gradually, in successive drops and at fitting times; an overwhelming descent could destroy what it strikes and turn benefit into harm.
rows.anchor: فنزل دفعة واحدة فأهلك ما نزل عليه فزالت المفقرة وعادت المنفعة مضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heaven is the high place where continuous rainfall would not be stopped without an overpowering authority.
rows.anchor: أي المحل العالي الذي لا يمسك فيه الماء عن دوام التقاطر إلا بقاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blessed water is exceedingly beneficial and enduring, encompassing human benefits rather than being an illusion.
rows.anchor: أي نافعا جدا ثابتا لا خيالا محيطا بجميع منافعكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water causes things to form and consolidate into wood, grain, grapes, and other wondrous growths.
rows.anchor: كان الماء سببا في تكون الأشياءن وكان ذلك سببا في انعقاده حتى يصير خشبا وحبا وعنبا , وغير ذلك عجبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb uses the majestic plural nūn, presenting the making of gardens as God's act.
rows.anchor: { فأنبتنا } معبرا بنون العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gardens include fruit trees, crops, and other growth gathered in orchards that conceal those who enter.
rows.anchor: من الثمر والشجر والزرع وغيره مما تجمعه البساتين فتجن - أي تستر - الداخل فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harvest grain means plants such as wheat and barley whose grain is harvested and whose stalks feed livestock.
rows.anchor: أي النجم الذي من شأنه أن يحصد من البر والشعير ونحوهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These grains are more valuable than pearls grown by rain because they sustain plants and provide food, while pearls serve adornment.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الحبوب أشرف من حب اللآلىء الذي ينبته الله نم المطر لأنها لقيام النبتة ؟ وتلك للزينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Date palms are especially wondrous and useful trees, tall above other fruit trees and bearing good fruit.
rows.anchor: أي عاليات طويلا على جميع الأشجار المثمرة ذوات أثمار طيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The compact spadix is the palm's emerging upper growth, with its load layered between coverings and a tapered tip.
rows.anchor: أي مصفوف متراكم بعضه فوق بعض , وهو حشو طلعه , والطلع ذلك الخارج من أعلى النخلة كأنه فعلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ṭalʿ is the first fruit showing; its casing, called kafrī, covers it securely.
rows.anchor: الطلع ما يبدو من ثمر النخل أول ظهورها , وذلك القشر يسمى الكفرى لتعطيته إياه على أحكم مما يكون وأوثق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Palm fruit develops varied colors, has food and enjoyment uses, and differs from most trees whose fruits grow separately.
rows.anchor: وهي محيطة المنافع بالتفكه على عدة أنواع والاقتيات وغير ذلك , وطلعها مخالف لعادة أكثر الأشجار فإن ثمارها مفردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God caused these plants to grow because they form part of the provision He assigned to His servants.
rows.anchor: أي أنبتنا به ذلك لأجل أنه بعض ما جعلناه رزقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine ending in town signals its extreme weakness and need for support and stability.
rows.anchor: وسمها بالتاء إشارة غلىأناه في غاية الضعف والحاجة إلى الثبات والخلو عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the town dead further stresses how fully dependent it is on revival.
rows.anchor: للزيادة في تقرير تمكن الحاجة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plants emerging from pulverized earth resemble the dead rising from graves, restored as they were in worldly life.
rows.anchor: أي مثل هذا الإخراج العظيم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān pairs heaven's construction, adornment, and lack of fissures with earth's spreading, mountains, and sprouting; he also compares their structural relations.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : ذكر تعالى في السماء ثلاثة : البناء والتزيين ونفي الفروج , وفي الأرض ثلاثة : المد وإلقاء الرواسي والإنبات , قابل المد بالبناء

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān notes crops harvested annually while the plant remains, crops sown every year or two, and mixed produce; crops are mostly staple food while fruits may be food or delight.
rows.anchor: ونبه فيما تعلق به الإنبات على ما يقطف كل سنة ويبقى أصله , وما يزرع كل سنة أو سنتين ويقطف كل سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted wish to receive good from God on return is denied: the speaker will not get what he wants, proving his subjection to the sole sovereign.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الاستفهام إنكاريا , كان المعنى : ليس له ما تمنى , وكان ذلك دليلا قطعيا على أنه مربوب مقهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole dominion belongs to God alone.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك دليلا قطعيا على أنه مربوب مقهور ممن له الأمر كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is where pleasures, fulfilled wishes, and their deprivation reach full realization; idolaters imagine their gods will intercede and make them prosper there.
rows.anchor: دار اللذات وبلوغ جميع الأماني وحرمانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is mentioned first because only those who follow guidance and resist desire attain their wishes there; nobody attains every wish in worldly life.
rows.anchor: فهو لا يعطي الأماني فيها إلا لمن تبع هاده وخالف هواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordering is semantic, not for rhyme, since al-ukhrā would also have suited the rhyme.
rows.anchor: فلهذا قدمها لا للفاصلة فإنه لو قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even the honored angels in heaven cannot avail anyone through intercession on their own.
rows.anchor: أي عن أحد من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that intercession neither benefits, suffices, compensates, nor meets a need.
rows.anchor: أي لا تجزي وتسد وتكفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception limits the negation: intercession only avails after divine permission, not as an independent power.
rows.anchor: ودل بإثبات الجار على أنه مع ما يحده سبحانه لا مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction with an and a verb indicates permission is renewed on each occasion, not granted universally for all times.
rows.anchor: وعبر بأن والفعل دلالة على أنه لا عموم بعد الإذن بجميع الأوقات , وإنما ذلك يجدد بعد تجدد الإذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's will determines either who may intercede or who may receive intercession.
rows.anchor: أي بتجدد تعلق مشيئته به لأن يكون مشفوعا أو شافعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike a human king who might permit intercession unwillingly, God must approve; then an authorized angel's intercession can avail.
rows.anchor: فحينئذ تغني شفاعتهم إذا كانوا من المأذون لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deny the afterlife call the angels female, claiming they are God's daughters.
rows.anchor: بأن قالوا : هي بنات الله , كما يقال في جنس الأنثى : بنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have no knowledge supporting the names they assign to the angels.
rows.anchor: أي بما سموهم به , وأعرق في النفي بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They act as if certain their beliefs benefit them, though their basis is conjecture alone.
rows.anchor: ولما كانوا كالقاطعين بأن ذلك ينفعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating الظن instead of using a pronoun emphasizes that conjecture cannot replace truth.
rows.anchor: ولذلك أظهر في موضع الإضمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conjecture cannot yield certainty; it is barred in foundational creed, while authorized, conditioned conjecture is used in practical rulings because humans cannot be certain in every branch.
rows.anchor: والظن إنما يعبر به في العمليات لا العلميات ولا سيما الأصولية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone owns every entity and meaning in the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: من الذوات والمعاني فيشمل ذلك السموات والأراضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens contain one another and the earth is in the heavens; the whole is under the Throne of the Lord of the mighty Throne.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الأراضي والكل في العرش وهو ذو العرش العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because all things belong to God, the Prophet may turn away from opponents; God could have guided them, but His wisdom leaves their dispute in place.
rows.anchor: فلو شاء لهداهم ورفع النزاع , ولكنه له في ذلك حكم تحار فيها الأفكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author connects this instruction to the earlier command in al-Jāthiya that believers forgive their opponents.
rows.anchor: علل الإعراض كما تقدم في الجاثية في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will requite wrongdoers for their misguidance, relieving the Prophet of concern about their fate.
rows.anchor: أي يعاقب هو سبحانه كافيا لك ما أهمك من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment may come through the Prophet and believers' swords when God permits fighting, through death at angels' hands, and through all sins being punished in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: إما بواسطتك وبسيوفك وسيوف أتباعك إذا أذنت لكم في القتال , وإما بغير ذلك بالموت حتف الأنف بضرب الملائكة وجوههم وأدبارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, since God owns all things, He governs them by assigning each person the recompense deserved; judgment follows ownership.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التقدير : وكما أنه سبحانه مالك ذلك فهو ملكه ليحكم بجزاء كل على حسب ما يستحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewards those who remain steadfast in religion and endure their enemies' abuse with the most excellent lasting recompense.
rows.anchor: أي على ثباتهم على الدين وصبرهم عليه وعلى أذى أعدائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥusnā is the feminine form of al-aḥsan, denoting the unsurpassed best outcome.
rows.anchor: ما بعدها غاية , فإن الحسنى تأنيث الأحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who do good exert themselves to avoid major sins and indecencies.
rows.anchor: أي يكلفون أنفسهم ويجهدونها على أن يتركوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Major sins are offenses the revealed law marks as grave through a threat of punishment or a legal penalty.
rows.anchor: أي ما عظم الشارع إثمه بعد الحريمه بالوعيد والحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Indecencies are major offenses rejected by natural disposition and reason and regarded as vile.
rows.anchor: والفاحشة من الكبائر ما يكرهه الطبع وينكره العقل ويستخسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads the exception as disconnected: minor slips are forgiven, and those who fall into them remain among the people of good.
rows.anchor: من أحسن , فهو استثناء منقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls the exception disconnected, yet notes that a minor sin can become major when treated lightly, as in the cited warning about slander.
rows.anchor: ولعله وضع فيه { إلا } موضع { لكن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lamam means minor sins, especially occasional slips that happen without deliberate choice, not a repeated practice or habit.
rows.anchor: ما يحصل منها في الأحيان كأنه وقع في صحابه فلتة بغير اختيار منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated or habitual minor wrongdoing is excluded from the pardon being described.
rows.anchor: أو يكثر حتى يصير كالعادة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says the root sense is approaching a sin, then refraining before committing it.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : وأصله مقاربة الذنب ثم الامتناع منه قبل الفعل

rows.speaker: ذو النون
rows.claim: Dhū al-Nūn says that an accomplished gnostic's mention of an indecency is like another person's committing it.
rows.anchor: قال ذو النون : ذكر الفاحشة من العارف كفلعها من غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression ألم بالمكان means to stay only briefly in a place.
rows.anchor: يقال : وألم بالمكان - إذا قل لبثه فيه

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ defines lamam as a person falling into a sin and then not repeating it; al-Suddī transmits the answer through al-Baghawī.
rows.anchor: وقال البغوي : قال السدي : قال أبو صالح أنه سئل عن اللمم فقال : هو الرجل يلم بالذنب ثم لا يعاوده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When Abū Ṣāliḥ shared that definition, Ibn ʿAbbās praised it, saying a noble angel had helped him.
rows.anchor: فذكرت ذلك لابن عباس رضي الله عنهما فقال : لقد أعانك عليها ملك كريم

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī says the root idea is an act done from time to time without repeating it or persisting in it, which allows a connected exception.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا يصح أن يكون الاستثناء متصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls the exception disconnected, while noting that al-Baghawī's account also permits treating it as connected.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا يصح أن يكون الاستثناء متصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God truly forgives minor sins and may forgive major ones; unlike human kings, His forgiveness is not limited by fear of losing control of His realm.
rows.anchor: فهو يغفر الصغائر حقا أوجبه على نفسه ويغفر الكبائر إن شاء بخلاف غيره من الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows people themselves and their condition, countering the assumption that He knows them only through their deeds or that readers can certify themselves as righteous.
rows.anchor: أي بذواتكم وأحوالكم منك بأنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created humanity through Adam from earth, whose cold and dry character is associated with death; human capacities had not yet emerged to disclose what each person would become.
rows.anchor: التي طبعها طبع الموت : البرد واليبس

words: وَإِذْ أَنتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌۭ فِى بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The womb language specifies the hidden embryos in their mothers' bellies, where the four temperaments arise after the elements mix.
rows.anchor: فكانت هذه الأربعة الأخلاط الزكية والدنية , ولكن لا علم لكم أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God already knows each person's future good or evil, even if their conduct later seems different; people do not know what is within themselves.
rows.anchor: فهو يعلم إذ ذاك ما أنتم صائرون إليه من خير وشر وإن عملتم مدة من العمر بخلاف ذلك فإنه يعلم ما جبلكم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should not boast about virtue because humans love status out of deficiency and a person's course can change before death.
rows.anchor: ولما كان من عادة من سلم من الذنوب أن يفتخر على من قارفها لما بني الإنسان عليه من محبة الفخر

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī explains self-purification as praising oneself for purity and says doing so signals being veiled from God.
rows.anchor: فإن تزكيته لنفسه من علامات كونه محجوبا عن الله - قال القشيري -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning can also cover praising a fellow believer, since praise may prove false and cause harm.
rows.anchor: أو مجازا بأن يثني على غيره من إخوانه فإنه كثيرا ما يثني بشيء فيظهر خلافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He invokes a hadith warning that a person may do the deeds of the people of Paradise until near its end, yet their outcome can change.
rows.anchor: العبد ليعمل بعمل أهل الجنة حتى ما يكون بينه وبينها إلا باع أو ذراع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows who struggles against the self until attaining piety and gives that person more reward in both worlds than expected, especially when piety becomes settled.
rows.anchor: فهو يوصله فوق ما يؤمل من الثواب في الدارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rescued Noah by carrying him on water after the whole face of the earth became one expanse of water.
rows.anchor: على متن ذلك الماء بعد أن صار جميع وجه الأرض مجرى واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ark is described as having broad planks made from sawn timber.
rows.anchor: أي أخشاب نجرت حتى صارت عريضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disur are fasteners joining the planks, such as iron or wooden nails or palm-fiber ropes, providing strength and firmness.
rows.anchor: ما يشد به السفينة وتوصل بها ألواحها ويلج بعضها ببعض بمسمار من حديد أو خشب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boat itself is left unnamed so readers will identify it by reflecting on its description.
rows.anchor: وحذف الموصوف تهويلا بالحث على تعرفه بتأمل الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description displays God's power to separate what is joined and join what is split, shaping a crafted object for an immense purpose.
rows.anchor: تنبيها على قدرته على ما يريد من فتق الرتق ورتق الفتق بحيث يصير ذلك المصنوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ark runs under God's watch and protection from entering the sea of darkness or suffering other calamities, as something constantly observed.
rows.anchor: حفظ من ينظر الشيء كثرة ولا يغيب عنه أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reading of the phrase takes eyes as a broken plural meaning springs or sources of water.
rows.anchor: وجوزوا أن يكون جمع تكسير لعين الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ark's protection is Noah's recompense; the wording also warns hearers that rejecting God's greatest blessing brings punishment.
rows.anchor: ليحذر السامع وقوع مثل ذلك العذاب له إن وقع منه مثل فعل قومه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid's active-voice reading fits taking the referent as Noah's people, whose disbelief is portrayed as ingrained in them.
rows.anchor: لتوافق قراءة مجاهد بالبناء . للفاعل . ولما تم الخبر عن نجاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ark's extraordinary voyage and preservation of its kind were left as a sign of God's knowledge and power.
rows.anchor: أي هذه الفعلة العظيمة من جري السفينة على هذا الوجه وإبقاء نوعها دالة على ما لنا من العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the very ark remained on al-Jūdī until later people of this community saw its remnants.
rows.anchor: وقيل : تلك السفينة بعينها بقيت على الجودي حتى أدرك بقايا ما هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign calls people to work at remembering and to give thanks to the Creator according to the guidance of His messengers.
rows.anchor: أي مجتهد في التذكير بسبب هذا الأمر لما يحق على الخلق من شكر الخالق بما هدت إليه رسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question reproaches deniers and asks how God's punishment and warnings actually came to pass.
rows.anchor: أي لمن كذب وكفر وكذب رسلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nudhur can refer both to God's warnings and to the messengers who convey them.
rows.anchor: الإنذارات الصادرة عني والمنذرون المبلغون عني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saved Noah, his believing children and others, then destroyed their enemies; all people now descend from Noah.
rows.anchor: فإنه أنجى نوحا عليه السلام ومن آمن معه من أولاده وغيرهم ومتعهم

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī sees strong hope for believers facing religious hardship: God can destroy their enemies and give them their lands and homes.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : في هذا قوة لرجاء أهل الدين إذا لقوا في دين الله محنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning repeats after earlier stories so listeners of every age and level may learn how God seized their peoples and benefit from messengers' warnings.
rows.anchor: وكان المعنى في تكرير ذلك عليهم بعد التذكي بما أتيناهم به من قصص هذه الأمم ميسرا لفهم صغيرهم وكبيرهم وذكرهم وأنثاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The detailed stories were among the early Quranic material, made accessible to ease the community's learning.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هذا التفصيل مما أنزل أول القرآن تيسيرا على الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Facilitating the Quran for remembrance includes admonition, recollection, reflection, understanding, memorization, and honor for those who attend to it.
rows.anchor: أي الاتعاظ والتذكر والتدبر والفهم والحفظ والتشريف لمن يراعيه

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Barrajān says the Arabic Quran was sent for understanding, addressed people in familiar ways, and taught them through examples.
rows.anchor: قال ابن برجان : أنزلناه باللسان العربي وأنزلناه للأفهام تنزيلا وخاطبناهم بعوائدهم

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī says recitation, knowledge, understanding, and memorization are made easy for different people, all of whom are the Quran's chosen people.
rows.anchor: وقال القشيري : يسر قراءته على ألسنة قوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could have spoken in eloquent expressions no one understood, but instead used the most eloquent accessible language; this accessibility alongside unsurpassed eloquence is miraculous.
rows.anchor: لجئناهم بعبارات لا يشمون رائحتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran translates God's acts in the visible and unseen worlds and explains the divine names and attributes by which He makes Himself known.
rows.anchor: من أسمائه الحسنى وصفاته العليا التي تعرف لنا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings encompass traces of God's acts within themselves, enabling reflection on the Quran.
rows.anchor: فما من شيء من أفعاله إلا وفي نفسه منه أثر ظاهر ناظر للتفكر في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance recalls what a person once knew but forgot and cannot summon independently until reminded.
rows.anchor: لما كان الإنسان يعرفه ثن نسيه حتى صار لا يستقل باستحضاره فإذا ذكر به ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing question appeals to people to remember what God has made accessible for them to recall.
rows.anchor: فقال منبها على عظيم فعل العلم والقرآن الذي هو طريقه بالتكرار والتعبير

rows.speaker: مطر الوراق
rows.claim: Al-Bukhārī quotes Maṭar al-Warrāq glossing the question as asking whether there is a seeker of knowledge who will be helped.
rows.anchor: قال مطر الوراق : هل من طالب علم فيعان عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder recurs four times in this surah; its final line appears separately from Quranic facilitation twice, at the Noah opening and after Pharaoh's story.
rows.anchor: وقد تكررت هذه الموعظة في هذه السورة أربع مرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase Which of your Lord's favors will you deny? recurs thirty-one times in al-Raḥmān.
rows.anchor: في الرحمن إحدى وثلاثين مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author speculates that the reminder alludes to five consecutive surahs and their endings; repeated letters, reversal, and assimilation point to the five senses as beginnings of knowledge.
rows.anchor: فكانت هذه الكلمة التي مدلولها الذكر مشيرة إلى الحواس الخمس الظاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He treats the first and last reminder clauses, omitting Quranic facilitation, as corresponding to two boundary letters assimilated into one and therefore to a single verse among the four.
rows.anchor: وكان ما في أول هذه المواعظ وآخرها لخلوه عن ذكر القرآن موازيا للحرفين اللذين طرفهما للوهن بالتعبير والقلب لكن كان الحرفان بالإدغام كحرف واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing Judgment, the author says God's decree encompasses everything, including disbelievers' persistence; some wrongly infer God approves their conduct.
rows.anchor: ولما أخبر بقيام الساعة وما يتفق لهم فيها جزاء لأعمالهم التي قدرها عليهم وهي ستر فرضوا بها لاتباع الشهوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created every small and great thing according to fixed measure: decree, judgment, proportion, bounded allotment, governance, and planning at a set time and place, written in the Preserved Tablet and measured by angels.
rows.anchor: أي قضاء وحكم وقياس مضبوط وقسمة محدودة وقودة بالغة وتدبير محكم في وقت معلوم ومكان محدود مكتوب في ذلك اللوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative in كل شيء signals universal scope; the following clause resumes the omitted governing verb and describes creation as precisely ordered.
rows.anchor: استأنف قوله تفسيرا للعامل المطوي وإخبارا بجعل ذلك الخلق كله على نظام محكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rebukes people who accepted sinful acts as God's will and then used it to excuse themselves, quoting their claim that God would not have allowed idolatry if He wished otherwise.
rows.anchor: فاصبروا عليه وارضوا به كما كنتم ترضون أعمالكم السيئة ثم تحتجون على عبادنا بأنها مشيئتنا بنحو
